2. Brief facts for filing of this appeal are that on 10.06.2013 at about 17.50 hours the deceased Haseenabanu and her husband got down from KSRTC bus at Shivamoga circle and were going towards their house.
At that time, one tractor bearing No.KA-17/TB-2396 came from Bongale circle towards bypass road in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against Haseenabanu.

In the result,
Haseenabanu sustained fatal injuries and she was shifted to Government Hospital, Harihar and thereafter shifted to SSIMS Hospital, Davanagere, there she took treatment from 10.06.2013 to 27.06.2013.
Thereafter she was shifted to KMC Manipal and took treatment from 27.06.2013 to 10.07.2013 and then shifted to City Central Hosptial, took treatment from 10.07.2013 to 28.07.2013.
While undergoing treatment, Haseenabanu succumbed to the injuries on 28.07.2013.
3. It is averred that the claimants have spent money on the deceased for the treatment and for funeral expenses.
It is also averred that deceased was hale and healthy prior to the accident and she was the only bread earner of the family.
It is further averred that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of tractor.
The legal heirs of the deceased Haseenbanu filed a claim petition under section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 for the death of Haseenbanu.
4. The respondent No.1 being the owner of the tractor bearing No.KA-17/TB-2396 filed objection statement denying the age, avocation and earnings of the deceased.
It is contended that the deceased was negligently crossing the busy road and at that time, the accident occurred.

It is also contended that the driver of the tractor was having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the tractor is insured with respondent No.2 and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. The insurer of offending vehicle i.e., tractor, filed objection statement contending that the driver of the tractor was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

It is averred that the respondent No.1 being the owner of the said vehicle knowing fully well the said fact had allowed the driver to take the vehicle on the road, hence he has committed breach of policy conditions.
It is further averred that the compensation claimed by the claimants is excessive and exorbitant and prays for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. The Tribunal has framed the issues and recorded the evidence of the parties.
The claimant No.1 examined himself as PW-1 and marked Exs.P-1 to P-36.
The respondents neither examined any witness nor marked any documents on their behalf.

On appreciation of the material on record, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.2,39,944/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation on the following heads:

Learned counsel Sri Anjaneya M. for appellant/claimants submits that the deceased was doing tailoring work and to establish the same,
the claimants have produced Ex.P-33, certificate issued by the Directorate of Civilian Bengaluru,
Davanagere District Administration for deceased having taken training in tailoring and garments work from 13.01.2004 to 28.04.2008.
He further submits that the Tribunal has committed error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- p.m. as she was doing tailoring work and earning Rs.12,000/- per month.
He further submits that the Tribunal has committed error in not adding 10% to the assessed income towards future prospects of the deceased as she was aged about 53 years as on the date of accident.
He sought for enhancement of compensation on other heads.

8. Per contra, learned counsel Sri A.G. Jadhav for insurance company supports the impugned judgment and award and submits that the Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the claimants were not depended upon the earnings of the deceased and has rightly assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month by applying proper multiplier and awarded Rs.2,39,944/- which is just compensation, the same does not call for any interference in the present appeal.
9. We have heard the learned counsels for the appellants and the respondent No.2, perused the memorandum of appeal and the Tribunal records.

The points that arise for consideration in the present appeal are :
1. Whether the Tribunal is justified in holding that the appellants are not the dependents of the deceased ?
2. Whether any enhancement is required to be made in the present appeal?
10. The answer to point No.1 is answered in the negative and point No.2 in the affirmative for the following reasons:
11. There is no dispute with regard to the accident resulting in death of deceased Haseenabanu, who is wife of the appellant No.1 and mother of appellant No.2, in a road accident that took place on 10.06.2013.
It is also not in dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 herein.

Insofar as the finding of the Tribunal that the appellant No.1 is the husband of the deceased Haseenabanu and appellant No.2 is the son, the relationship of the deceased with the appellants-claimants is not disputed by the respondent-insurance company.

However, insofar as the dependency of the appellants- claimants upon the deceased is concerned, the appellant No.1 is a retired employee of the Birla Company, he has received retiral benefits and every month he gets Rs.1,400/- as pension and as per the cause title, the appellant No.2 is aged about 20 years and doing Allabaksha S/O Abdul Razaksab vs G. Sharanappa S/O Shivanagouda on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90326062/
4
private job being an able bodied person, capable of earning independently and having his independent source of income, cannot be considered as dependent of the deceased Haseenabanu.
12. In our considered view, the said finding of the Tribunal is contrary to the evidence on record and settled position of law.

The finding of the Tribunal that appellant Nos.1 and 2 have independent source of income may be partially true, however, the contribution of the deceased Haseenabanu,
who was the wife of appellant No.1 and mother of appellant No.2, has definitely required to be - 10 - taken into consideration as she has substantially contributed to the upliftment of the family as a whole.
The appellant No.1 being the husband of the deceased is getting meager pension of Rs.1,400/- per month.

The said pension amount would not be sufficient to maintain the entire family, and no contrary evidence is placed on record by the respondent-insurance company about the independent income of the appellants.
Hence, the said contention of the respondent-insurance company has no merit.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kirti and another Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited1, at paragraph Nos.17 to 21 and 25 and 30 held as under:
"17.

entities.text: Kirti and another Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are two distinct categories of situations wherein the Court usually determines notional income of a victim.
The first category of cases relates to those wherein the victim was employed, but the claimants are not able to prove her actual income, before the Court.

In such a situation, the Court "guesses" the income of the victim on the basis of the evidence on record, like the quality of life being led by the victim and her family, the general earning of an individual employed in that field, the qualifications of the victim, and other considerations.
The second category of cases relates to those situations wherein the Court is called upon to determine the income of a nonearning victim, such as a child, a student or a homemaker.
Needless to say, compensation in such cases is extremely difficult to quantify.

19. The Court often follows different principles for determining the compensation towards a non- earning victim in order to arrive at an amount which would be just in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Some of these involve the determination of notional income.
Whenever notional income is determined in such cases, different considerations and factors are taken into account.

[See M. R.
Krishna Murthi v. New India Assurance Co. Ltd., 2019 SCC OnLine SC 315]

One category of nonearning victims that Courts are often called upon to calculate the compensation for are homemakers.
The granting of compensation for homemakers on a pecuniary basis, as in the present case, has been considered by this Court earlier on numerous occasions.

A threeJudge Bench of this Court in Lata Wadhwa v. State of Bihar, (2001) 8 SCC 197, while dealing with compensation for the victims of a fire during a function, granted compensation to housewives on the basis of the services rendered by them in the house, and their age.

entities.text: Lata Wadhwa v. State of Bihar, (2001) 8 SCC 197
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court, in that case,
held as follows:
"10.

So far as the deceased housewives are concerned, in the absence of any data and as the housewives were not earning any income, attempt has been made to determine the compensation on the basis of services rendered by them to the house.

On the basis of the age group of the housewives, appropriate multiplier has been applied, but the estimation of the value of services rendered to the house by the housewives,
which has been arrived at Rs - 12 - 12,000 per annum in cases of some and Rs 10,000 for others, appears to us to be grossly low.

It is true that the claimants, who ought to have given data for determination of compensation, did not assist in any manner by providing the data for estimating the value of services rendered by such housewives.

But even in the absence of such data and taking into consideration the multifarious services rendered by the housewives for managing the entire family, even on a modest estimation,
should be Rs 3000 per month and Rs 36,000 per annum..."
(emphasis supplied)

21. In Arun Kumar Agrawal v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., (2010) 9 SCC 218, this Court, while dealing with the grant of compensation for the death of a housewife due to a motor vehicle accident,
held as follows:
"26.

entities.text: Arun Kumar Agrawal v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., (2010) 9 SCC 218
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In India the courts have recognised that the contribution made by the wife to the house is invaluable and cannot be computed in terms of money.
The gratuitous services rendered by the wife with true love and affection to the children and her husband and managing the household affairs cannot be equated with the services rendered by others.
A wife/mother does not work by the clock.
She is in the constant attendance of the family throughout the day and night unless she is employed and is required to attend the employer's work for particular hours.
She takes care of all the requirements of the husband and children including cooking of food, washing of clothes, etc.
She teaches small children and provides invaluable guidance to them for their future life.

A housekeeper or maidservant can do the household work, such as cooking food, washing clothes and utensils, keeping the house clean, etc., but she can never be a substitute for a wife/mother who renders selfless service to her husband and children.

- 13 - Allabaksha S/O Abdul Razaksab vs G. Sharanappa S/O Shivanagouda on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90326062/
6 27.

entities.text: Abdul Razaksab vs G. Sharanappa S/O Shivanagouda
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is not possible to quantify any amount in lieu of the services rendered by the wife/mother to the family i.e. the husband and children.
However, for the purpose of award of compensation to the dependants, some pecuniary estimate has to be made of the services of the housewife/mother.

In that context, the term "services" is required to be given a broad meaning and must be construed by taking into account the loss of personal care and attention given by the deceased to her children as a mother and to her husband as a wife.
They are entitled to adequate compensation in lieu of the loss of gratuitous services rendered by the deceased.

The amount payable to the dependants cannot be diminished on the ground that some close relation like a grandmother may volunteer to render some of the services to the family which the deceased was giving earlier."
(emphasis supplied)

The above pronouncement has been followed by this Court in its recent judgment in Rajendra Singh v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., 2020 SCC OnLine SC 521, wherein the notional income of a deceased housewife was calculated for the purposes of granting compensation in a motor accident case."

sentences.text: The sheer amount of time and effort that is dedicated to household work by individuals, who are more likely to be women than men, is not surprising when one considers the plethora of activities a housemaker undertakes.

A housemaker often prepares food for the entire family, manages the procurement of groceries and other household shopping needs, cleans and manages the house and its surroundings, undertakes decoration, repairs and maintenance work,
- 14 - looks after the needs of the children and any aged member of the household, manages budgets and so much more.

30. The issue of fixing notional income for a homemaker, therefore, serves extremely important functions.
It is a recognition of the multitude of women who are engaged in this activity, whether by choice or as a result of social/cultural norms.
It signals to society at large that the law and the Courts of the land believe in the value of the labour, services and sacrifices of homemakers.

It is an acceptance of the idea that these activities contribute in a very real way to the economic condition of the family, and the economy of the nation, regardless of the fact that it may have been traditionally excluded from economic analyses.
It is a reflection of changing attitudes and mindsets and of our international law obligations.
And, most importantly, it is a step towards the constitutional vision of social equality and ensuring dignity of life to all individuals.

13. In the instant case, the deceased had definitely contributed her services and income to the family and due to the sudden death of deceased Haseenabanu, vacuum - 15 - has been created in the family not only with regard to love and affection, but the income and support to the family by the deceased.
Hence, in our considered view, the Tribunal has committed error in holding that the appellants are not dependents on the deceased Haseenabanu.
14. The Tribunal in the absence of any cogent and acceptable evidence has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- p.m.
In our considered view, the notional income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal is on the lower side.

This Court and Lok-adalaths while settling the disputes under the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, base its reliance on the notional income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authorities.
As per the chart, the notional income for the accidents taken place in the year 2013 is to be assessed at Rs.7,000/- p.m.

In our considered view, in the absence of any cogent and acceptable evidence on record, basing our reliance on the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, we assess the notional income of - 16 - the deceased at Rs.7,000/- p.m.
The Tribunal has committed error in not awarding the compensation under the head of future prospects.

Keeping in mind the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others2, we deem it appropriate that the appellant-claimants are entitled for addition of 10% to the assessed income towards future prospects as the deceased was aged about 53 years at the time of accident and was self-employed.

Thus, the appellants- claimants are entitled for loss of dependency as under:

The appellants are entitled for Rs.15,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses and a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Magma Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram and others3, the appellant No.1 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards spousal consortium and appellant No.2 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards parental consortium.
